messages:
Anya: quick heads-up: ran into an attribution mismatch during a local canary. When both an org-level API key and a project-specific key are present in the same request, the router sometimes favors the org. This is causing project dashboards to under-report usage and org dashboards to inflate.
Sam: can you paste the minimal repro headers?
Anya: sure:
```
Authorization: ApiKey org=org_42; key=abc123
X-Forwarded-Project: proj=proj_99; key=xyz987
```
runtime parsing currently accepts the first authenticated principal it finds, and because the proxy injects the org header earlier, it wins.
Miguel: that aligns with the alert noise I saw — project quota alerts firing despite console showing low project consumption. We need clearer telemetry before flipping heuristics.
Anya: proposal: prefer explicit project-scoped keys when both present. Order: project > service_account (acting_on_project) > org. Also emit both the selected principal and full candidate chain in traces/metrics so dashboards can break down ambiguous cases.
Sam: two implementation notes: (1) existing token caches are keyed by org for perf; if we change resolution we must avoid cache collisions. (2) how do we detect delegated SA acting_on_project vs a plain SA?
Anya: for (1) we'll add scope to cache key: e.g., `auth_cache:v2|{model}|{scope_type}:{id}` so org vs project entries are separate. For (2) we already have claim `act_as_project` in the SA token; runtime will treat SA with that claim as project-scoped.
Miguel: from observability: add metric `auth.attribution` (values: project|org|sa|ambiguous) and `auth.candidate_chain` (CSV of candidates). I'll add a Grafana panel and an alert if ambiguous ratio > 3% during canary.
Rebecca: product flag: if we change attribution, customers could see sudden spikes on project billing. Recommend roll as runtime feature-flag behind an admin toggle and a 2-step console notice: a short banner on affected project dashboards for 48h plus an email to org owners if delta > 5%.
Anya: agreed. Roll plan: introduce runtime feature flag `prefer_project_attribution` default=false. Enable for 5% traffic in us-west1 for 24h. Collect metrics and billing-delta samples, then increase to 50% for 24h before global. Also console will surface an "Attribution migration" banner when flag toggled org-wide.
Sam: I'll add unit tests for header parsing precedence and integration tests exercising cache namespace variants. Also add a staging-only toggle that simulates previous behavior for diff testing in CI.
Miguel: I'll wire telemetry ingestion and a quick dashboard that shows per-project vs org attribution over time + ambiguous cases. Hook an alert: if ambiguous_count / total_requests > 0.03 in canary, abort rollout.
InfraBot: canary-deploy initiated by @miguel — id cny-2026-03-21-09, target 5% traffic in us-west1. Logs forwarded to #build-failures per usual.
Anya: created tracking ticket infra/attr-preference-2026 and pushed runtime PR with flag + tests. Pushing console banner PR shortly.
Rebecca: drafting banner copy now: "Attribution update: weve improved how requests are attributed between org and project API keys. You may see temporary changes to project usage during the rollout. Learn more."
Sam: note: ensure backward compatibility for customers relying on org-first behavior (rare but possible). Keep flag off by default and expose admin control.
Anya: yep. I'll add migration notes to release notes and the admin guide. Will update thread after canary metrics come in. :thumbsup:
